instructions: Cut the paneer into pieces about 3/4 inch by 2 inches and pat them dry. Slice the onion and both peppers into strips about 1/4 inch thick. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add the paneer in a single layer and cook for about 4 minutes, turning once or twice, until golden in spots. Transfer it to a plate and sprinkle with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Turn the heat down to medium and add the remaining 2 tbsp oil and the cumin seeds. After about 30 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty.
Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt. Cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and light golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until they smell fragrant.
Turn the heat to low and add the chili powder, ground coriander and turmeric. Stir for 20 seconds, then add the crushed tomatoes and the sugar right away.
Turn the heat up to medium-high and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and the oil shows at the edges.
Add the peppers and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until they're slightly tender but still a little crisp. If the pan dries out, add 1 to 2 tbsp water.

Turn the heat to low. Crush the kasuri methi between your palms over the pan, then add the garam masala, the paneer and the last 1/4 tsp salt. Stir gently to coat the paneer, cover and cook for 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the vinegar and 2 tbsp chopped cilantro. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a splash more of the vinegar.
method_notes: Swasthi's (the lead) is the quickest: onion and a tomato puree masala with chili, garam masala and kasuri methi, then peppers kept crisp and paneer folded in last. Cooking and Me browns the paneer first and adds nigella seed, and Archana's Kitchen adds carrots and a little honey. This one follows Swasthi's order, browns the paneer the Cooking and Me way, and leaves out the hot chilies so the pot stays mild.
